references.text: Earlier in the chapter, the Gibeonites describe their worn-out sacks and cracked wineskins as part of their deception, which verse 13 elaborates on further.
A parallel verse describing the dry and moldy bread, part of the same deception where the Gibeonites pretend to have traveled a long distance.
Moses reminds the Israelites that their clothes did not wear out during the wilderness journey, in contrast to the Gibeonites' claim about worn-out clothing.
God's miracle that clothes and shoes did not wear out in the wilderness stands in contrast to the Gibeonites' false claim of wear from a long journey.
Nehemiah refers to the same miracle that clothes and shoes did not wear out, which the Gibeonites tried to exploit in their deception.
